description: To introduce the concept of information security, and number theory. To make students familiar with different aspects of access control, system security and its applications. To make students familiar with various cryptographic algorithms. To design security solutions for different operation systems and networks.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Information Security
syllabus.body: Meaning of information security, privacy, vulnerability, threat, attack, CIA Triad, CNSS Security Model, components of an information system, OSI Security Architecture, model for network security, network access security model, access control.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Number Theory
syllabus.body: Divisibility, Division Algorithm, Euclidean Algorithm, Extended Euclidean Algorithm, fast exponentiation algorithm; modular arithmetic, congruences, Chinese Remainder Theorem, algebraic structures, Galois Fields.

syllabus.title: Introduction to Cryptography
syllabus.body: Private key cryptography: traditional symmetric-key ciphers, modern symmetric key ciphers, DES, AES, block cipher modes of operation; public key cryptography: trapdoor one-way function, RSA, Diffie-Hellman key exchange, cryptographic hash function, digital signature.

syllabus.title: System and Operating Security
syllabus.body: Overview, security policy, file protection mechanisms, user authentication, security models, trusted operating system design, host based and network based intrusion detection and prevention systems.

syllabus.title: Network Security
syllabus.body: Network security concepts, network threats, security controls, firewalls, protecting programs and data, secure program, sniffing, spoofing, non malicious program errors, malware, viruses and other malicious code, control against programs, honeypot, SDN security, IoT security.

outcomes: Able to understand the information security and number theory concepts.
Able to analyse different aspects of access control, system security and its applications.
Able to understand and analyse various cryptographic algorithms.
Able to design and develop security solutions for different operating systems and networks.
textbooks: Charles P. Pfleeger, Share Lawrence Pfleeger, Security in Computing, Pearson Education, 2/e.
William Stallings, Cryptography and Network Security, PHI, 7/e.
B.A. Forouzan, Cryptography and Network Security, McGraw-Hill, 3/e.
referenceBooks: Charlie Kaufman, Perlman & S Peeciner, Network Security, Pearson Education, 2/e.
